## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noVueVForTemplateKeyOnChild`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**error**](/reference/diagnostics#error).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/no-v-for-template-key-on-child`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/no-v-for-template-key-on-child)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueVForTemplateKeyOnChild": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow placing the `key` of a `<template v-for>` on its child elements.

When a `<template>` tag repeats its content with `v-for`, Vue expects the `key`
on the `<template>` tag itself. A `key` on a child element that uses the loop
variables belongs on the `<template>` tag instead.

Child elements that have their own `v-if`, `v-else-if`, `v-else`, or `v-for`
are not reported, and neither are keys that don't use any variable from the
`<template>`'s `v-for`.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <template v-for="todo in todos">
    <TodoItem :key="todo.id" />
  </template>
</template>
```

<Fragment set:html={"<pre class=\"language-text\"><code class=\"language-text\"></code></pre>"} />

### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <template v-for="todo in todos" :key="todo.id">
    <TodoItem />
  </template>
  <template v-for="todo in todos" :key="todo.id">
    <TodoItem v-if="todo.visible" :key="todo.id" />
  </template>
</template>
```
